engagement.model: Human eosinophils and Th2 cells in vitro

engagement.judgement: Opens the strip with a member drug (AZD1981); fevipiprant and QAV680 were profiled in the same human eosinophil/Th2 assays (Sandham 2013, 2017). engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT01545726 posted no results.
engagement.model: Human eosinophils and Th2 cells in vitro
engagement.note: Retrodiction: fevipiprant cut sputum eosinophils 3.5-fold vs placebo in eosinophilic asthmatics, after OC000459 had already done so in patients.
engagement.quote: Compared with baseline, mean sputum eosinophil percentage was reduced by 4·5 times in the fevipiprant group and by 1·3 times in the placebo group (difference between groups 3·5 times, 95% CI 1·7-7·0; p=0·0014).
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison: the in-vitro model predicts blocked eosinophil recruitment, and sputum eosinophils are a downstream readout of it. No member reported ex-vivo whole-blood shape change in dosed humans in an abstract I could read, so no direct-tier entry. MK-1029 allergen-challenge sputum eosinophil data (NCT01343407, results 2019-02-08) are later and were not read. Ruling: retrodiction. OC000459 had already cut sputum eosinophils and ex-vivo blood eosinophil shape change in asthmatics (Singh 2012, epub 2012-04-10), before this model result was public; engagement counts any drug's earlier patient result. Model side for this track is fevipiprant's own human eosinophil/Th2 profile (Sykes 2016, epub 2016-02-25), so product_in_model true. The checker's 2014 ARRY-502 adjudication is a different drug's track under the track rule and is appended as its own entry rather than moving this entry's year.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract does not name the species or readouts.
efficacy.note: QAV680, a member, was effective in rodent CRTh2-dependent mechanistic and allergic disease models before entering asthma trials.

efficacy.quote: The molecule exhibited good oral bioavailability in the rat, combined with efficacy in rodent CRTh2-dependent mechanistic and allergic disease models and was suitable for clinical development.
efficacy.judgement: model_first_use_year 2009 is a proxy: QAV680 entered asthma trials (NCT00814216, completed 2009-10) on these data, published only in 2013. AZD1981 could not be tested in mouse or rat cells, which did not respond to DP2 agonists (Schmidt 2013), so the rodent model's relevance is itself doubtful.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The rodent model was run on QAV680, not AZD1981.
efficacy.note: AZD1981 added to background ICS/LABA (not a combination arm) missed its FEV1 primary in 1,140 asthmatics; a retrodiction that failed.
efficacy.quote: However, the improvement for the highest AZD1981 dose (400 mg BID) vs placebo was not statistically significant (0.02 L, P=0.58), preventing interpretation of statistical testing for the lower doses.
efficacy.judgement: Dated to the registry posting of NCT01197794 (2013-09-10), the first public in-class primary-endpoint result. Later member trials split: BI 671800 met its FEV1 primary (Hall 2015, +3-4% predicted) and fevipiprant met it in dose-ranging (Bateman 2017), but a failed model stays failed and one drug's contra beats another's same. Phase 3 confirmed the miss (LUSTER, ZEAL). Ruling: retrodiction. Patient FEV1 results for DP2 antagonism (OC000459, Barnes 2011, epub 2011-07-15) were public before this model result; efficacy counts any drug's earlier patient result. It failed to reproduce this member's result, so contra. BI 671800 and fevipiprant are split onto their own tracks at the end of the cell.

patient_trials.quote: Following 4 weeks of treatment, there was a nonsignificant increase in morning peak expiratory flow on AZD1981 1,000 mg bid (9.5 L/min vs placebo, P=0.086 [study 1] and 12 L/min vs placebo, P=0.16 [study 2]).
These findings suggest that BI 671800 is associated with a small improvement in FEV1 in symptomatic controller-naïve asthma patients, and in patients on ICS.
There were no significant differences between QAW039 and placebo for trough forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) or Asthma control questionnaire (ACQ) in the total population.

Fevipiprant produced a statistically significant improvement in the primary end-point of change in pre-dose forced expiratory volume in 1 s at week 12 (p=0.0035) with a maximum model-averaged difference to placebo of 0.112 L.

Although neither trial showed a statistically significant reduction in asthma exacerbations after adjusting for multiple testing, consistent and modest reductions in exacerbations rates were observed in both studies with the 450 mg dose of fevipiprant.
Although GB001 did not significantly reduce the odds of asthma worsening, reductions favoring GB001 were observed.

Sibling-drug pairing as in the main strip. It failed to reproduce this member's result, so contra. MK-1029's own track is appended at the end of the cell.

safety.model: Off-target selectivity panels; animal toxicology unpublished
safety.note: AZD1981 was clean on over 340 enzymes and receptors; no member's animal toxicology or regulatory review is public.
safety.short: Clean selectivity panel; tox never public
safety.quote: Binding was reversible, non-competitive and highly selective against a panel of more than 340 other enzymes and receptors, including DP1 (>1000-fold selective).
safety.judgement: No member was filed with FDA or EMA (manifest: no NDA/BLA), so no review names the toxicology package. Patient safety was placebo-like for fevipiprant (LUSTER serious AEs 9% in every arm), but GB001 60 mg carried a risk of liver injury (Moss 2022). With no public GB001 preclinical toxicology I cannot say whether the model was silent or stated a margin, so the hepatic signal is left unscored rather than called contra.
